business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Brokerage of Ginned Raw Cotton and Synthetic Yarns

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state legal or tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law - code-based, French-tradition unitary system, with commercial company law codified in the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-Uzbekistan Agreement on Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 4 October 2009, in force 2010) - relevant for Central Asian raw-cotton sourcing
Luxembourg-Hong Kong Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (in force 2005)
Luxembourg-United States Double Taxation Convention (in force 1996, as amended)
Luxembourg-People's Republic of China Double Taxation Convention (in force 1994, as amended by 2007 protocol)
EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement and EU Generalized Scheme of Preferences (Regulation (EU) No 978/2012) governing eligible cotton-supplier states

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, as amended; SARL governed by Articles 710-1 et seq. and general provisions of Articles 1, 2, 5, 126 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés du Luxembourg (RCS Luxembourg), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), through the eJustice.lu online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of association (acte constitutif / statuts) filed electronically with the RCS by the Luxembourg notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A SARL must have a minimum issued and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000. Cash contributions must be deposited before incorporation into a blocked account (compte bloqué) with an approved Luxembourg credit institution and are released to management only upon RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS OF [LU SARL]. RESOLVED, that the subscribers and initial board hereby (i) approve the subscription of [100] shares at €[120] each, representing the fully paid-up share capital of €12,000; (ii) adopt the registered office at [Address], Luxembourg, as filed with the RCS; (iii) appoint [Name] as Manager and authorised sole representative, with full power to register the company and open bank accounts; and (iv) authorize any additional corporate actions and signatures necessary for the completion of incorporation and the commencement of the international cotton brokerage activity. This resolution is effective as of the date of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Luxembourg / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), eJustice.lu portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online to reserve the name [Company Name] SARL and obtain a certificate of name reservation. Simultaneously prepare the draft articles of association and select the registered office address. Ensure the name does not conflict with existing protected names or trademarks.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application
Draft articles of association
Identity copy of intended managers and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a trademark or user similarity objection is raised, file a new reservation within 10 days using a distinctive prefix or suffix.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and deposit of EUR 12,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the SARL in formation ('SARL en formation'). Deposit at least EUR 12,000 as cash contribution. The bank issues a blocking certificate ('attestation de blocage') to be produced to the notary. Retain the certificate until RCS registration, then request release of funds.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name reservation
Passport of beneficial owner and managers
Bank account application and KYC/AML forms
Business plan and economic substance information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional economic substance or source-of-funds evidence, provide the lease agreement and client or supplier contracts, or select another Luxembourg bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) selected by the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the notarized articles of association before a Luxembourg notary. The deed must include the fully subscribed paid-up capital, registered office address, manager(s), corporate purpose (international brokerage and export of ginned raw cotton and synthetic yarns under ISIC 4620), and the management authority. The notary delivers a certified copy for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Blocking certificate from the bank
Lease agreement or domiciliation letter for the registered office
Draft articles of association
Valid passport or identity documents of all signatories and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues observations, amend the relevant articles and sign a rectification deed; notary fees are adjusted accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS filing, registration number, and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) eJustice platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the deed and the RCS registration form (formulaire C) electronically. Pay the RCS registration fee. Once verified, the RCS allocates the Luxembourg registration number and registers the legal form 'SARL'. The deed is published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), conferring legal effect to third parties.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
RCS filing form (formulaire C)
Manager's consent letter and residence certificate
Proof of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS asks for clarification, respond through the notary or directly within 15 days; after rectification the file is treated as if the defect had never existed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation registrations: VAT, social security, and municipal establishment permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); commune of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL for Luxembourg VAT using the RCS extract; register employees with the CCSS for social insurance; obtain a municipal autorisation d'établissement (business licence) for the commercial brokerage office. For raw cotton brokerage and export, no sectoral industrial licence is required.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (certified)
Articles of association and incorporation deed
Registered office lease and fire certificate
Manager passport and criminal record extract
Bank account activation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the establishment permit, file a settlement appeal with the Minister of the Economy or the commune appeal board; for VAT queries, respond to AEDT within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (Directorate-General for Industry) - not applicable to a pure international brokerage and export entity without manufacturing or warehouse installations in Luxembourg
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required; only the standard business licence (autorisation d'établissement) from the commune of the registered office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not applicable - office-based brokerage and export of ginned raw cotton bales; no physical manufacturing, coating, or effluent-producing installation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no wastewater or VOC point sources. If warehousing is added, compliance with EU Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) and Luxembourg Water Act limits for any incidental sanitary effluents would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (attestation de sécurité incendie) issued by the local commune / CGDIS fire and rescue service for the registered office; structural load sign-off if storage area exceeds 200 m²; occupational workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration; all filings and registrations effected via the MyGuichet.lu national e-government portal and the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate SARL before the Luxembourg notary and register with the RCS to obtain the national identification number (matricule d'identification, 11-digit 'L' prefix). 2) File the electronic VAT registration application (Formulaire 640) with the AEDT simultaneously with the RCS filing, or within 15 days of the first taxable transaction. 3) Foreign non-EU entities must appoint a Luxembourg-established VAT fiscal representative (assujetti établi) and provide apostilled incorporation documents, Articles of Association, and proof of the beneficial owner's identity for AML verification. 4) Register for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax via ACD Form 1/registration questionnaire once the RCS matricule is issued; 5) Acquire the EORI number (European Union Registration and Identification) from the Customs and Excise Agency to lodge export declarations; 6) The completed TIN/VAT ID is issued electronically within 2-4 weeks of submission of full documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: Luxembourg-resident SARL is taxable on worldwide income at entity level at the aggregate standard rate of 24.94% (Luxembourg City, comprising 17% corporate income tax, 7% municipal business tax on taxable basis adjusted to 3.5%, and 0.2475% solidarity surcharge). No pass-through or fiscal transparency for SARL; the company is an autonomous subject of tax. Exemption for qualifying participation (≥10% or €1.2M acquisition cost, held ≥12 months) under the participation exemption regime, and no withholding tax on dividends qualifying under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg domestic law does not provide a check-the-box election; SARL is mandatorily entity-level taxed. Available elections: (1) Group taxation (régime d'intégration fiscale) election for 95%-owned resident subsidiaries (full tax consolidation); (2) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Article 61 VAT law for closely linked resident entities; (3) Co-ownership (copropriété) treatment or tax-transparent FCP/SCSp is not available to SARL; (4) US tax purposes: eligible as a US check-the-box non-per se corporation election to be treated as partnership/disregarded entity, subject to Treasury Reg. §301.7701-3; (5) Hybrid mismatch: Luxembourg has transposed ATAD (Law of 21 December 2018) incorporating EU anti-hybrid rules; no elective carve-out exists except grandfathered instruments existing before 1 January 2017 and pre-ATAD structures protected until 31 December 2021; mismatches triggered by the SARL must be neutralised by the payor rule regardless of jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small business exemption (Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law) — however, the threshold does not apply to export/brokerage of goods without established place of supply in Luxembourg; registration is mandatory from the first transaction if the SARL is established in Luxembourg (no threshold benefit for export activities where input VAT recovery is sought).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time tax-authority fiscal clearance (no French-style FADETTE or Italian regime) — Luxembourg mandates B2G e-invoicing via the PEPPOL network (Peppol BIS 3.0) for all invoices to central public administration and municipal authorities; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary but all received e-invoices must be accepted; issuance of structured EDI/e-invoice requires prior AEDT approval for EDI-based systems; invoices must contain the RCS matricule and the VAT ID; self-billing and invoicing by the third-party appraiser are permitted; all export invoices must be retained in original format for 10 years (Article 72 VAT Law). No digital stamping requirement for paper invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies under Article 41.I of the Luxembourg VAT Law to supplies of goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU by the supplier, the customer, or a third party acting for them, including the international brokerage of raw cotton bales (ex-Quotation 4620) where the broker's service is directly linked to the exported goods and the goods never enter the Luxembourg domestic supply chain; alternative zero-rating applies to intra-EU dispatch (Article 43) subject to the customer providing a valid VIES VAT number; the zero-rating is conditional exclusively on the SARL holding contemporaneous documentary evidence of the physical movement of the goods across the EU external border or the customer's registration in the destination EU state, and on the invoice issuing within 15 days of the supply of services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique / SAD — Form EX-A and the electronic AES export declaration lodged via Luxembourg Customs IT system), bearing the MRN (Movement Reference Number) and final non-EU destination customs office of exit

Bill of Lading (for ocean freight) or CMR consignment note (for road transport to non-EU border such as Belarus/Russia) or Air Waybill (for air cargo), evidencing the actual departure of the cotton bales from the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/FX confirmation from the bank evidencing the USD/EUR wire transfer received from the non-EU buyer, matching the invoice value and shipment date

Incoterms-Dated Commercial Invoice (with explicit 'Exported from EU / Taxé 0%' annotation), Packing List, Certificate of Origin, and the Buyer's written Purchase Order confirming the non-EU destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT customs audit unit performs ex-post validation of export documentation samples; if the SARL cannot produce the complete bundle within the 10-year retention period or if transport documents are not dated within 90 days of the invoice, the zero-rating is reversed and the entire VAT in dispute becomes immediately payable with retrospective effect up to 5 years (extended to 10 years in cases of tax fraud or intentional deception); administrative penalty of 10% of the underestimated tax plus late interest of 0.6% per month; for deliberate falsification of the export evidence, criminal prosecution under Article 49 VAT Law triggers fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, plus publication of the judgment; the ACD may additionally reassess corporate income tax on the same transaction under Article 60-AO; under the EU anti-fraud programme, the transaction is cross-checked against the VIES and the customs trader files (ECS) — a missing reconciliation of AES exit confirmation automatically triggers the withdrawal of the exporter status and application of 17% VAT with clawback of input credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the authorized prudential and AML/CFT supervisor of credit institutions, payment institutions, and e-money institutions. Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration; exchange-control functions are subsumed under BCL monetary-policy operations and CSSF licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions within the Eurozone. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls, no prior payment authorizations, no currency quotas, and no foreign-exchange licensing for trade settlements. Profit remittance is unrestricted: dividends bear the standard Luxembourg withholding tax of 15%, fully reduced to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate parents under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU); no additional central-bank approval is required. Free movement of capital is guaranteed under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg exporters may retain 100% of export proceeds in euro or any freely convertible foreign currency without mandatory conversion to euro, without surrender deadlines, and without export-deposit requirements. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL is required for material cross-border goods flows and direct-investment movements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs without a Luxembourg or EU/EEA license cannot legally provide payment services to a Luxembourg SARL under PSD2. Feasibility rating: Low for non-passported offshore EMIs. Only CSSF-licensed Luxembourg EMIs or EU/EEA-passported digital banks may operate, and they typically impose stricter-than-average entity-level KYC. Feasibility rating for EU-passported digital EMIs: Medium, contingent on the EMI offering a substantive Luxembourg servicing channel, SWIFT-correspondent coverage, and acceptance of the SARL's raw-cotton trade documents.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF Regulation 18/698, banks must positively identify the SARL, its directors, and its beneficial owners. In practice, at least one duly authorized director or manager must attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises or before a Luxembourg notary; remote video onboarding is accepted only when supported by a CSSF-approved qualified electronic identification (eIDAS) or an equivalent certified digital identity, and non-EU corporate documents require notarized, apostilled, and officially translated copies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty exposure to cotton-producing jurisdictions with elevated corruption, sanctions, or trade-transparency risk (e.g., Central Asia, West Africa, East Africa)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply-chain KYC pack: contractual chain from ginning mill to FOB port, independent origin certificates and internationally classed cotton certificates (e.g., CAI/ICA), chamber-of-commerce abstracts, real-time UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screening results, bank reference letters for each material supplier, and a signed four-eyes compliance opinion from the SARL's RCSI (Responsable du respect des obligations).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice valuation outliers versus Cotlook A Index or ICE cotton futures without documented grade, quality, or freight differentials
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party price-benchmark reports, broker mandate agreement evidencing commission basis, bills of lading, origin and weight certificates, quality survey reports (e.g., USDA or CAI class certificates), and customs-validated export declarations (SAD) for each shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement instructions or payment routing through unrelated intermediary accounts in jurisdictions outside the transaction chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented chain-of-payment rationale, full corporate organigram and UBO register filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), trade-finance instruments (LC/DC) evidencing the underlying commercial transaction, and SWIFT cover-payment records showing the complete correspondent route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners, signatories, or counterparties connected to politically exposed persons (PEPs) or sanction-listed entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP status declarations and negative-news search results, independent source-of-wealth files (audited financials, contracts, tax returns, bank statements), ongoing transaction-monitoring framework adopted by the bank, and global sanctions-screening certificates covering all transactional counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate transaction velocity on a newly incorporated SARL account featuring rapid in-and-out fund movements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury mandate and projected cash-flow model, forecast trade volumes under cotton brokerage and export agreements, continuously updated AML/KYC file maintained by the RCSI, and designation of a dedicated compliance contact for the bank's relationship team.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholders inject equity via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wires into the notarial blocked-funds account (compte de blocage) opened for the SARL; each wire must cite the incorporation deed reference, the notary's account details, and the statutory purpose code. Under BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting, capital contributions are classified under direct-investment code EO 438. The receiving bank requires source-of-funds evidence (shareholder reserves, audited financials, purchase agreements); upon issuance of the notarial certificate and registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), funds are released to the operational account. All inbound wires are sanctions-screened and matched to the constitutive instruments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement to international cotton suppliers and yarn mills is executed through: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct telegraphic transfers in EUR or USD; (ii) irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit issued by a Luxembourg bank under UCP 600, frequently confirmed by a bank in the supplier's jurisdiction; and (iii) documentary collections under URC 522 for risk-compressed transactions. Each payment instruction references the commercial invoice number, underlying contract, and bill of lading; outbound payments are screened against UN, EU, and OFAC sanctions lists, benchmarked against invoice valuation, and matched to transport and quality documentation before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward contracts (plain vanilla, tenor aligned to LC maturities, typically 30-180 days)
EUR/USD foreign-exchange swaps (FX swaps) for short-term liquidity matching between receivable and payable cycles
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for hedging long-term trade-finance liabilities and structural working-capital exposures
Vanilla EUR/USD FX options where bank ISDA/EMIR documentation permits

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted emerging-market currencies (e.g., UZS, NGN) solely where a confirmable underlying cotton receivable or payable in that currency is evidenced by the trade contract

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convene and hold Ordinary General Meeting for approval of annual accounts and discharge of managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; minutes retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year-end (balance sheet date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting within the statutory window exposes managers to civil liability; shareholders may petition the commercial court to order the meeting; the filing of annual accounts with the RCS is blocked until approval is obtained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: File approved annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss statement, annex) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via the eJustice.lu platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the general meeting; approval must occur no later than six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar issues a compliance order with a three-month filing deadline; continued default is punishable by coercive fines (astreinte) imposed by the court, criminal fines, public disclosure of non-compliance, and personal liability of managers for resulting damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: File annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax return (form C)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year companies, subject to the tax filing notice and customary extension requests
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to 10% of assessed tax; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; missed filings allow the tax authority to issue estimated assessments, which are immediately enforceable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: File annual net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – net wealth tax unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the corporate income tax return, typically 31 December of the following year for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The annual minimum net wealth tax of EUR 535 remains due; late filing attracts penalties of up to 10% plus monthly interest of 0.6%; enforcement includes attachment of bank accounts and assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Submit annual confirmation of beneficial owners to the Luxembourg RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the ordinary general meeting approving the annual accounts; if no meeting is held, within one month after the statutory deadline for approval of the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation leads to inclusion on the public RBE non-compliance list; criminal fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 and may be imposed separately on each director; repeated violations aggravate administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé is mandatory for SARLs exceeding at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50 employees. SARLs below all thresholds are exempt from statutory audit but still must have accounts prepared and approved by shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial companies and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for non-public-interest entities and is mandatory for consolidated financial statements of EU-listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: After each ordinary general meeting approving the annual accounts, the manager (gérant) must confirm the RBE record, including the identity and extent of ownership or control of each beneficial owner. Any transfer of shares, creation of pledges, or change in the nature of beneficial ownership must be reflected in the RBE within one month of the event. Share transfers become enforceable against the company only once recorded in the register of members.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 20,000 (only when statutory thresholds are exceeded; small SARLs are exempt)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined effective headline rate for Luxembourg City (15% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, 6.75% communal business tax; CIT rate 15% applies to taxable income above EUR 200,000, with 4.1% on the first EUR 175,000 and 4.55% on the EUR 175,000-EUR 200,000 band)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box regime (80% exemption on qualifying net IP income, effective rate approximately 5%); investment tax credit (credit d'impôt investissement) of 8% for eligible tangible/intangible assets with enhanced rates for SMEs and environmental investments; participation exemption under Article 147 LIR for qualifying dividends and capital gains where the SARL holds at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million of the participating capital for at least 12 months; notional interest deduction for equity increases; special tax regime for shipping or IP may reduce effective cash tax to the 4.1%-16.05% municipal-CIT band
